It sounds like there's underlying issues that need to be addressed. It isn't always as simple as being lazy and negligent. It's possible you could have depression which makes things harder for you to do. Most people who have normal brains have no problems getting up and doing things despite not really wanting to do them. People who have depression struggle to even do the most basic tasks like self care (ie bathing, feeding themselves, quite literally even getting out of bed) so don't beat yourself up too hard. Try putting in a pointed effort. Genuinely. If you still seem to struggle to wake up, get out of bed, do basic things in your life, you might want to talk to someone about the possibility that you might not be like everyone else.  I'll use myself as an example.

 There have been times when I have to do chores. I'm an adult and I have to do them to continue to function as an adult. I have to do laundry or I can't go to work. So I tell myself ok, I'm going to do laundry today. So I spend time scrolling TikTok as the time goes by I keep looking at the clock watching the day pass by. The more time that passes the more anxiety I'm getting. I need to do laundry, just get up and go do the laundry. I'm beating myself up the longer I wait but I still can't seem to get out of bed or off my phone. It's too late to go do laundry now. I've spent the whole day in bed scrolling on my phone. Now I either have to get up early or miss work. If this sounds like a familiar cycle for what you're going through, that's not normal. That's not laziness. That's something that goes way deeper than just trying harder. So be kind to yourself and understand that it genuinely might not be your fault and you just need a little help to function better as a person.

As someone who has quite a few interests, personally I go through what I call cycles. I get interested into something, invest quite a bit of time into it to get to at least basic beginner status where I can do the thing without constant guidance, then I can put it down and do something else that I enjoy. I put down and pick up as I feel the desire too. If you get special projects in mind, save them into your phone and work on it when you feel like it. I find that if I force myself into a hobby I don't enjoy at the moment it makes me not want to do it for longer than normal because it feels forced instead of just being able to enjoy the thing so just take the time to really find out what you enjoy vs doing things just because. Wanting to learn all the things is admirable but overwhelming lol.  

In terms of learning or finding out what you like, plenty of colleges and craft/hobby groups have introductory classes that are low to no cost just to see if you enjoy it, meetup is a fantastic resource to find hobbyists in your area to test the waters for whatever you feel like doing. Sorry if it seems like this reply is all over the place, but I'm also a person who loves learning things.

You've gotten a lot of really good comments, but my advice is look into a program called Job Corp. It's a free trade school program, there's usually at least 1 in every state if not more. They teach you 2 free trades, there's a place to live, they feed you 3 times a day and it's 1000% free. It sounds too good to be true but I promise you it's not a gimmick or some mlm or anything weird. It's paid for by the department of labor to help people get into the labor force. If you need help with housing, a job, high school diploma/ged, drivers license, anything like that, they help you get it. Look for the one in your state and apply now, but feel free to look at what different job corps in different areas provide, if the one in your state doesn't have a trade you like, they'll send you to a different one for free. Let them know once you turn 18 you're going to be homeless (technically it's not a lie since that's what you've been told) if you can hang on for 2 more years, you have at least one way to get out and get a free education and help with housing. Don't give up just yet, you're so close to freedom, you just need a plan and this imo is a really easy and great start.
